issues.legal_issue: A prosecution’s suppression of the occurrence’s origin and failure to explain serious injuries, including a death, on the accused side may require acquittal rather than conviction on the basis of a free fight.
material_facts: The High Court noted that the parties disputed possession of the land where the occurrence took place and that the case arose from a cross-version.
The accused side had injuries, including serious head injuries to the appellants’ father, who later died, but the prosecution offered no explanation for those injuries.
The trial court did not discuss the defence evidence or exhibits concerning the accused side’s injuries.

The Supreme Court found that the prosecution had suppressed the origin and genesis of the occurrence and that the circumstances were not those of a free fight in which witnesses could not reasonably be expected to see and explain the defence injuries.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not sustain the convictions by treating the case as a free fight; the appellants were entitled to the benefit of doubt and were acquitted of all charges.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle applied in Lakshmi Singh and others v. State of Bihar, unexplained injuries on the accused side may support an adverse inference against the prosecution, particularly where the prosecution has suppressed the origin and genesis of the occurrence. The exception associated with a free fight applies where the occurrence may take place at different spots or in circumstances in which witnesses could not reasonably be expected to see and explain the defence injuries. The Court relied on no specific statutory provision as the basis for this principle.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and prosecution_suppressed_occurrence_genesis and prosecution_failed_to_explain_defence_injuries and serious_or_fatal_defence_injury and not free_fight_observation_exception

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal by an accused challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.prosecution_suppressed_occurrence_genesi: The prosecution failed to disclose the origin and genesis of the occurrence.
predicates.prosecution_failed_to_explain_defence_in: The prosecution did not explain injuries sustained by people on the accused side.
predicates.serious_or_fatal_defence_injury: A person on the accused side sustained a serious or fatal injury during the occurrence.
predicates.free_fight_observation_exception: The occurrence took place in circumstances, such as at different spots, in which a witness could not reasonably be expected to see and explain the injuries on the accused side.

issues.definition: When a conviction appeal concerns a prosecution that suppressed the occurrence’s genesis and left serious or fatal injuries on the accused side unexplained, and the circumstances do not make those injuries unobservable to witnesses, the accused are entitled to acquittal.

issues.legal_issue: A person may claim a right to use force when they see their parents being assaulted, particularly where the assault is shown to have caused a parent’s later death.
material_facts: The appellants’ father sustained head injuries during the occurrence and later died.
The Court stated that the appellants could claim a right to use force once they saw their parents being assaulted.
issues.conclusion: The appellants could legitimately claim a right to use force in the circumstances described; the appeal was allowed and they were acquitted of all charges.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that a right to use force could legitimately be claimed where the accused saw their parents being assaulted and the assault was shown to have caused their father’s later death. The judgment cited no specific statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this statement.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal by an accused challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_witnessed_parent_being_assaulted: The accused saw a parent being assaulted during the occurrence.
predicates.assault_caused_parent_fatal_injury: The assault caused an injury from which the parent later died.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction after seeing a parent assaulted and that assault caused the parent’s fatal injury, the accused may claim a right to use force.
